subject: MSA: Venue, Governing Law & Emergency Relief — AcmePay redlines
messages:
From: Sarah Nguyen <sarah.nguyen@acmepay.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: AcmePay Procurement <procure@acmepay.com>
Date: Sun, 5 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed MSA redlines — governing law and dispute resolution

Jordan / Laura —

Thanks for the draft. Procurement and our GC have reviewed the MSA and we have two primary concerns we need addressed before we can proceed: governing law and the path for emergency injunctive relief. High level:

- Governing law: AcmePay requires Delaware law for commercial contracts of this size, and we can't accept California law.
- Dispute resolution: we are fine with arbitration for most disputes, but need an explicit carve allowing us to seek injunctive or other equitable relief in court.

I've attached our annotated redlines (AcmePay_MSA_redlines_v1.pdf). Key asks are: Delaware governing law; exclusive jurisdiction in Delaware courts for actions seeking injunctive relief; arbitration (AAA) for other disputes with seat in New York.

Can you confirm Redwood's position on governing law and whether you can accept a narrow equitable-relief carve that specifies Delaware courts as the forum for emergency relief? If not, we need to understand alternatives so we can assess with our GC.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — procurement is trying to close this week.

Best,
Sarah Nguyen
Head of Procurement, AcmePay
attachments: AcmePay_MSA_redlines_v1.pdf (annotated PDF, 7 pages)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 6 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Proposed MSA redlines — governing law and dispute resolution

Looping you both in — AcmePay pushed back on CA law and wants Delaware + exclusive Delaware courts for injunctive relief. They also prefer AAA/New York for arbitration of other disputes.

My thinking: we should try to keep Redwood's preferred governing law (California) where possible because of our contracts team and precedent, but a small concession here is acceptable for a strategic customer. Suggested compromise: accept Delaware governing law, agree arbitration for most disputes (AAA, seat NY), but insert a narrowly tailored carve allowing either party to seek provisional or injunctive relief in the federal or state courts of Delaware (limited to equitable relief to preserve status quo) without waiving the arbitration requirement for other remedies.

Questions for legal: 1) do we need a reciprocal carve (i.e., allow Redwood the same right to seek injunctive relief in CA if needed)? 2) proposed clause language — see attached draft clause I jotted down (RWI-proposed-clause-Delaware-equitable-relief.docx).

Next steps: Laura / Markus, can you review and mark up? Procurement says they want to close this week so I'll try to keep communications tight.

Thanks —
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
attachments: RWI-proposed-clause-Delaware-equitable-relief.docx (word doc, suggested language)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: (internal only)
Date: Tue, 7 Jul 2026 14:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Proposed MSA redlines — governing law and dispute resolution

Jordan —

Thanks for the summary and the draft clause. From a legal risk perspective I recommend the following approach:

1) Governing law: Agree to Delaware law for this counterparty. We have several customers on Delaware law and it's acceptable.

2) Arbitration vs court carve: Accept arbitration for all disputes but insert a narrow, reciprocal equitable-relief carve. Suggested high-level language: either party may seek provisional or injunctive relief in the state or federal courts located in the State of Delaware to preserve the status quo pending resolution of the dispute; such actions shall not be deemed a waiver of arbitration and the underlying dispute will otherwise be resolved under the arbitration clause.

3) Venue specificity: For clarity, tie venue to the U.S. District Court for the District of Delaware for federal injunctive relief and to the Delaware Court of Chancery for certain equitable claims, but mark that as optional — if AcmePay pushes we can settle for "courts located in Delaware."

4) Practical tweak: add a notice-and-cure window (10 business days) before a party seeks injunctive relief except in cases where notices would be futile (e.g., imminent exfiltration or IP threats). This reduces emergency filings.

I'll mark the clause in the attached doc and prepare a clean MSA v3 to share with AcmePay. If procurement insists on non-reciprocal forum selection, elevate to me and Markus.

Laura Bennett
General Counsel, Redwood Inference
attachments: none

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Nguyen <sarah.nguyen@acmepay.com>, Tom Alvarez <t.alvarez@acmepay.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>, AcmePay Procurement <procure@acmepay.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Jul 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed MSA redlines — governing law and dispute resolution

Sarah / Tom —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the redlines. We appreciate AcmePay's position on Delaware law. Redwood is prepared to accept Delaware governing law for this agreement and to split the difference on dispute process as follows (summary, attached clean redline and a short clause excerpt):

- Governing law: Delaware law will govern the MSA.
- Arbitration: Commercial disputes arising out of or relating to the MSA will be submitted to final and binding arbitration administered by the American Arbitration Association (AAA) under its Commercial Arbitration Rules, with the seat of arbitration in New York, NY.
- Equitable relief carve: Either party may seek provisional, injunctive, or other equitable relief in a court of competent jurisdiction in the State of Delaware (including federal courts) to preserve the status quo pending arbitration or other dispute resolution. Such filings will not be considered a waiver of the requirement to arbitrate other claims.
- Venue note: For clarity, parties agree that federal courts in the District of Delaware (or state courts sitting in Delaware) are acceptable fora for equitable relief. We also included an optional 10-business-day notice-and-cure before seeking injunctive relief except where such notice would be futile.

Attached: MSA_clean_v3_for_acmepay.docx (clean redline with language accepted above). Please review and let us know if AcmePay can proceed on that basis; if so we can issue an updated DocuSign packet for signatures.

If you prefer a reciprocal carve that allows Redwood to seek injunctive relief in California courts for specific IP or data-protection emergencies, please flag and we can discuss. Our preference is the Delaware solution above to keep execution moving.

Best regards,

Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0192

attachments: MSA_clean_v3_for_acmepay.docx (clean redline), RWI-proposed-clause-Delaware-equitable-relief.docx (internal language suggestion)
